name: Pierre Auger Observatory

intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: Beginning of the construction of the observatory.

intervals.label: operations
intervals.note: Continuously operating since the November 2008 inauguration; the AugerPrime upgrade (2015-) proceeds concurrently with data taking. See experiment:pierre-auger-observatory for the richer history (partial-array data taking began in 2004, before the full 1660-tank array was complete).

summary.plain: A giant outdoor laboratory in the Argentine pampas that catches ultra-high-energy cosmic rays: tanks of water spread over an area the size of Rhode Island, watched by telescopes that see the faint light of particle showers in the night sky.
summary.technical: Hybrid ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory in Mendoza Province, Argentina, combining a 3000 km^2 surface array of 1660 water-Cherenkov detector stations with 27 fluorescence telescopes in four buildings overlooking the array; operated by the international Pierre Auger Collaboration since inauguration in November 2008, currently undergoing the AugerPrime upgrade.
